admet-reliability-2026.name: ADMET reliability benchmark
admet-reliability-2026.one_liner: Compares model families under limited data, unfamiliar molecular structures and class imbalance to assess ADMET prediction in practical research settings.
admet-reliability-2026.pain_point: Average benchmark scores miss reliability issues involving small datasets, out-of-distribution prediction, class imbalance, beyond-rule-of-five molecules and activity cliffs.
admet-reliability-2026.datasets: 14 property/ADMET datasets covering hERG, BBBP, Caco-2, half-life, VDss, CYP and peptide properties, plus 30 bioactivity tasks from MoleculeACE.
admet-reliability-2026.method: Compares KPGT, Uni-Mol, TabPFNv2, classical machine learning and AutoML in a common framework, using random, scaffold and Perimeter splits, resampling and ensembles.
admet-reliability-2026.conclusion: TabPFNv2 often performs well in the evaluated small-data/OOD settings. Undersampling ensembles help with imbalance, while KPGT performs strongly on cyclic-peptide permeability with more training data. Activity cliffs remain difficult across models.
admet-reliability-2026.evaluation: Uses random, scaffold and Perimeter splits, organizing experiments around small datasets, class imbalance and out-of-distribution prediction.
admet-reliability-2026.limitations: Table 1 and scenario-specific results show how model strengths change with data conditions. KPGT achieves R² = 0.627 on CycPept-PAMPA cyclic-peptide permeability.
admet-reliability-2026.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.
admet-reliability-2026.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, key sections of the paper and related official resources.

publication.citation: Journal of Cheminformatics 18, 95; 2026-05-18

caliciboost-2025.one_liner: Combines molecular fingerprints, physicochemical descriptors and automated machine learning to predict permeability through the Caco-2 intestinal cell model.
caliciboost-2025.pain_point: Caco-2 permeability data are limited and assay conditions vary, making it difficult to identify effective molecular features and modeling strategies.
caliciboost-2025.datasets: TDC Caco2_Wang contains 906 molecules. A separate OCHEM collection was reduced from 9,402 raw records to 5,481 modeling records through filtering and cleaning. The two datasets are modeled and evaluated separately.
caliciboost-2025.method: Compares fingerprints, RDKit/PaDEL/Mordred descriptors and CDDD representations, combining AutoGluon with feature selection, interpretation and hyperparameter optimization.
caliciboost-2025.conclusion: Feature selection and ensemble learning improve Caco-2 prediction. The official TDC Caco-2 leaderboard snapshot dated 2026-09-19 lists MAE = 0.256 ± 0.006 and ranks CaliciBoost first.
caliciboost-2025.evaluation: Evaluates TDC Caco2_Wang and the curated OCHEM data separately. The 2026-09-19 TDC snapshot reports MAE = 0.256 ± 0.006.
caliciboost-2025.limitations: Results illustrate the contribution of feature selection and ensembles. Some OCHEM records lack the assay direction, leaving label consistency as a data-quality issue.
caliciboost-2025.name: CaliciBoost
caliciboost-2025.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.
caliciboost-2025.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, key sections of the paper and related official resources.

publication.citation: Journal of Cheminformatics 17, 184; 2025-12-22; preceded by a 2025 preprint.

pksmart-2025.one_liner: Predicts animal pharmacokinetic parameters, then combines them with molecular features to estimate human intravenous clearance, distribution volume and half-life.
pksmart-2025.pain_point: Human PK data are scarce, limiting structure-only models. The study examines how preclinical species information can improve human parameter prediction.
pksmart-2025.datasets: Human intravenous PK data for 1,283 distinct compounds, covering VDss, clearance, half-life, unbound fraction and mean residence time; preclinical animal data for another collection of 371 compounds. Label availability varies by endpoint.
pksmart-2025.method: First predicts rat, dog and monkey PK parameters from molecular features, then combines these predictions with molecular features in human random-forest models. Uses repeated nested cross-validation and external validation.
pksmart-2025.conclusion: Reported external R² values are 0.39 for VDss and 0.46 for clearance, indicating that cross-species predictions can improve selected human PK endpoints.
pksmart-2025.evaluation: Repeated nested cross-validation and external validation; external R² is 0.39 for VDss and 0.46 for clearance.
pksmart-2025.limitations: The study concerns human intravenous PK. Two-stage model comparisons assess the contribution of animal PK information, while external R² values also show the remaining prediction error.
pksmart-2025.name: PKSmart
pksmart-2025.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.
pksmart-2025.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, key sections of the paper and related official resources.

publication.citation: Journal of Cheminformatics 17, 147; 2025-09-26

dcpm-admet-2026.one_liner: Combines representations from two pretrained models with chemical fingerprints to predict 97 ADMET properties.
dcpm-admet-2026.pain_point: A single representation struggles to capture semantic, structural and physicochemical information together, while ADMET labels are sparse and endpoints heterogeneous.
dcpm-admet-2026.datasets: Pretraining uses approximately 111 million PubChem records. The ADMET collection contains 97 endpoints: 43 regression and 54 classification tasks, with 465,470 endpoint records. Also evaluates 10 MoleculeNet datasets.
dcpm-admet-2026.method: Fuses XLNet semantic representations, a GRU component incorporating SMILES-to-InChI and property learning, and ECFP fingerprints; combines single-task random forests, multitask neural networks and parameter optimization.
dcpm-admet-2026.conclusion: Reports improvements over the ECFP baseline on 67/97 endpoints and the best results among compared methods on 5 of 10 MoleculeNet tasks.
dcpm-admet-2026.evaluation: Uses scaffold splits and model/feature comparisons; 67 of 97 endpoints outperform the paper's ECFP baseline.
dcpm-admet-2026.limitations: Fusion ablations examine the contribution of each representation. The platform offers 133 outputs: 97 model predictions and 36 calculated properties.
dcpm-admet-2026.name: DCPM-ADMET
dcpm-admet-2026.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.
dcpm-admet-2026.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, key sections of the paper and related official resources.

publication.citation: Journal of Cheminformatics 18, 126; 2026-06-20

kpgt-2023.one_liner: Incorporates fingerprints and physicochemical descriptors into graph pretraining to learn representations for ADMET and other molecular properties.
kpgt-2023.pain_point: Graph-pretraining objectives can diverge from downstream needs; representations must retain chemical knowledge and transfer effectively.
kpgt-2023.datasets: Approximately 2 million ChEMBL29 molecules for pretraining; 63 downstream datasets comprising 11 common property datasets, 22 TDC ADMET tasks and 30 MoleculeACE tasks.
kpgt-2023.method: Uses the LiGhT line-graph Transformer with descriptor- and fingerprint-guided pretraining, followed by downstream fine-tuning.
kpgt-2023.conclusion: Figure 2c and Supplementary Table 8 report the best performance among the models compared at publication on 16/22 TDC ADMET tasks.
kpgt-2023.evaluation: Evaluates TDC, MoleculeNet and MoleculeACE separately. Figure 2c and Supplementary Table 8 show the best compared results on 16 of 22 TDC tasks.
kpgt-2023.limitations: Pretraining uses approximately 2 million ChEMBL29 molecules; MoleculeACE further tests activity-cliff prediction. Ablations help assess knowledge-guided pretraining and downstream transfer.
kpgt-2023.name: KPGT
kpgt-2023.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.
kpgt-2023.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, key sections of the paper and related official resources.

publication.citation: Nature Communications 14, 7568; 2023-11-21. An earlier version appeared at KDD 2022; these notes cover the journal paper.

mole-2024.one_liner: Pretrains on a large collection of molecular graphs, adds supervised biological-task training, and fine-tunes for ADMET prediction.
mole-2024.pain_point: The study addresses how to learn transferable representations from very large unlabeled molecular collections and combine them with labeled biological information.
mole-2024.datasets: Approximately 842 million molecular graphs from ZINC20 and ExCAPE-DB for self-supervised learning, followed by supervised multitask pretraining; ADMET evaluation covers 22 TDC tasks.
mole-2024.method: Decoupled attention models atom content and relative graph position. Training proceeds from atom-environment prediction to supervised pretraining and downstream fine-tuning.
mole-2024.conclusion: Reports results exceeding the best published methods in a September 2023 TDC snapshot on 10/22 tasks, with means and standard deviations across multiple runs.
mole-2024.evaluation: Evaluates 22 TDC tasks over multiple runs; comparisons use a September 2023 snapshot of published TDC methods.
mole-2024.limitations: The paper describes excluding test molecules from pretraining. Reproduction also involves large-scale pretraining resources; checkpoint download instructions still contained a TODO when reviewed.
mole-2024.name: MolE
mole-2024.code_status: Implementation is public. Checkpoint download instructions contained a TODO when reviewed; availability of all weights is unconfirmed.
mole-2024.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, key sections of the paper and related official resources.

publication.citation: Nature Communications 15, 9431; 2024-11-12.

admet-ai-2024.one_liner: Packages graph neural networks into web and local tools that predict multiple ADMET properties for large compound libraries.
admet-ai-2024.pain_point: Large-scale screening requires accurate multi-endpoint predictions, high throughput and local deployment.
admet-ai-2024.datasets: 41 TDC prediction tasks: 31 classification and 10 regression tasks. Performance rankings use the 22-task ADMET Benchmark Group subset.
admet-ai-2024.method: The paper uses Chemprop D-MPNN with 200 RDKit descriptors, separate multitask classification and regression models, and model ensembles.
admet-ai-2024.conclusion: At publication, the authors reported a leading average TDC ADMET rank and high batch-processing efficiency, with both web and local tools available.
admet-ai-2024.evaluation: Training covers 41 tasks; performance rankings use 22 ADMET benchmark tasks. Figure 1B–C compares predictive performance and runtime.
admet-ai-2024.limitations: Inference speed depends on hardware and batch size. Version 2 changes the Chemprop version and feature configuration, so paper reproduction requires the corresponding software version.
admet-ai-2024.name: ADMET-AI
admet-ai-2024.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.
admet-ai-2024.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, key sections of the paper and related official resources.

publication.citation: Bioinformatics 40(7), btae416; online 2024-06-24; July 2024 issue.

mtgl-admet-2023.one_liner: Selects useful auxiliary tasks for each ADMET endpoint to reduce interference during multitask training.
mtgl-admet-2023.pain_point: Training all ADMET tasks together can cause negative transfer; each primary task may need a different auxiliary-task set.
mtgl-admet-2023.datasets: 24 endpoints collected from 8 publications: 18 classification and 6 regression tasks, covering 43,291 compounds and including ADMET plus 2 physicochemical endpoints.
mtgl-admet-2023.method: Uses state theory and maximum flow for auxiliary-task selection, together with shared atom representations, task-specific attention and a primary-task-centered gating module.
mtgl-admet-2023.conclusion: Comparisons and ablations show that adaptive task selection and gating improve prediction, supporting auxiliary-task selection tailored to the primary task.
mtgl-admet-2023.evaluation: Table 1 uses a random 8:1:1 split and 10 random seeds, with AUROC for classification and R² for regression.
mtgl-admet-2023.limitations: Comparisons focus on auxiliary-task selection and gating. The 24-endpoint collection differs from TDC's 22 tasks in data composition and splitting.
mtgl-admet-2023.name: MTGL-ADMET
mtgl-admet-2023.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.
mtgl-admet-2023.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, key sections of the paper and related official resources.

publication.citation: iScience 26(11), 108285; November 2023 issue. Preceded by a RECOMB 2023 conference paper.

himnet-2026.one_liner: Exchanges information across atoms, substructures and whole molecules in a hierarchical graph network for property and selected ADMET predictions.
himnet-2026.pain_point: Limited interaction across atom, substructure and molecular levels can leave property-relevant information out of single-level representations.
himnet-2026.datasets: 11 datasets: 8 MoleculeNet subsets plus Malaria, LMC and MetStab. BBBP, Tox21, SIDER, ClinTox and metabolic-stability tasks directly concern ADMET; others assess broader properties or bioactivity.
himnet-2026.method: Hierarchical message passing and attention combine directed message paths, cross-level interactions and consistency information from multiple fingerprints.
himnet-2026.conclusion: Tables 1–2 report best or near-best results on several tasks among the compared methods, supporting hierarchical feature fusion.
himnet-2026.evaluation: Tables 1–2 summarize 11 property/activity datasets. These notes cover the main comparisons; task-specific splits and hyperparameters remain to be added.
himnet-2026.limitations: Useful for studying hierarchical feature fusion alongside metabolic-stability tasks, especially how representations at different levels affect performance.
himnet-2026.name: HimNet
himnet-2026.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, key sections of the paper and related official resources.

publication.citation: Communications Chemistry 9, 150; 2026-02-14

molmcl-2025.one_liner: Learns molecular, scaffold and local-context representations, then combines them by task for property and bioactivity prediction.
molmcl-2025.pain_point: Tasks depend on different structural levels, making fixed graph representations and readouts difficult to adapt across tasks.
molmcl-2025.datasets: ZINC15 for pretraining; 7 MoleculeNet datasets and 30 MoleculeACE bioactivity tasks for downstream evaluation.
molmcl-2025.method: Multichannel learning over molecular, scaffold and contextual information, using molecular perturbations, contrastive learning and prompt-guided readout.
molmcl-2025.conclusion: Multichannel learning and task adaptation improve representations on the evaluated molecular tasks, with activity-cliff experiments demonstrating the design's value.
molmcl-2025.evaluation: Downstream experiments cover 7 MoleculeNet subsets and 30 MoleculeACE bioactivity tasks.
molmcl-2025.limitations: Activity-cliff experiments help examine representation sensitivity to local structural changes. This MolMCL and MoleMCL in Bioinformatics are separate studies.
molmcl-2025.name: MolMCL
molmcl-2025.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.
molmcl-2025.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, key sections of the paper and related official resources.

admetlab-3-2024.one_liner: Provides online ADMET and physicochemical predictions with uncertainty estimates, an API and decision-support tools.
admetlab-3-2024.pain_point: Limited property coverage, inconvenient access and point predictions alone constrain platform support for compound selection.
admetlab-3-2024.datasets: More than 400,000 records support model development; the platform provides 119 property/assessment outputs, including predicted endpoints and calculated properties.
admetlab-3-2024.method: Multitask directed message passing and descriptor-based modeling, combined with predictive uncertainty, API access and decision support.
admetlab-3-2024.conclusion: Expands property coverage and integrates batch processing, API access and uncertainty estimation for ADMET screening.
admetlab-3-2024.evaluation: These notes cover platform functions, data scale and modeling methods; endpoint-specific experimental settings remain to be added.
admetlab-3-2024.limitations: Platform comparisons can examine endpoint coverage, batch inference, uncertainty outputs and access options. See the review record for training-code and weight availability.
admetlab-3-2024.name: ADMETlab 3.0
admetlab-3-2024.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, abstract and accessible project documentation.

admetsar-3-2024.one_liner: Integrates ADMET data search, property prediction and structural optimization suggestions to help identify suitable candidates.
admetsar-3-2024.pain_point: Users need both property predictions and ways to find similar compounds and structural modifications that improve ADMET.
admetsar-3-2024.datasets: More than 370,000 experimental records covering 104,652 distinct compounds and 119 ADMET endpoints.
admetsar-3-2024.method: Multitask graph neural networks with database retrieval, similarity search, structural transformations and scaffold-hopping tools.
admetsar-3-2024.conclusion: Combines molecular exploration, property prediction and optimization suggestions in one platform for multiparameter screening and design.
admetsar-3-2024.evaluation: These notes cover data scale, prediction and optimization features; endpoint-specific experimental settings remain to be added.
admetsar-3-2024.limitations: The platform illustrates how to connect structural exploration, property prediction and optimization. Suggested molecules still require experimental assessment.
admetsar-3-2024.name: admetSAR3.0
admetsar-3-2024.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, abstract and accessible project documentation.

tdc-2021.one_liner: Organizes drug-discovery datasets and tasks into shared interfaces and benchmarks for consistent model comparison.
tdc-2021.pain_point: Fragmented datasets, task interfaces, splits and evaluation protocols make fair comparisons difficult.
tdc-2021.datasets: A collection spanning drug discovery and development. These notes focus on its 22-task ADMET Benchmark Group; the conference paper covers a broader set of tasks.
tdc-2021.method: Defines tasks, data interfaces, standardized benchmarks and public leaderboards.
tdc-2021.conclusion: Provides data loading, task splits and evaluation tools for comparing drug-discovery models under common settings.
tdc-2021.evaluation: The ADMET Benchmark Group uses task-specific metrics and scaffold splits, with evaluation across multiple random seeds.
tdc-2021.limitations: Toxicity tasks among the 22 endpoints include hERG, AMES, DILI and LD50. TDC also hosts other drug-discovery data; select tasks by benchmark group.
tdc-2021.name: TDC
tdc-2021.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, key sections of the paper and related official resources.

pharmabench-2024.one_liner: Uses language models to extract assay conditions, then cleans and harmonizes ADMET records to build better-specified benchmarks.
pharmabench-2024.pain_point: Inconsistent assay conditions and endpoint definitions reduce benchmark quality when labels are simply pooled.
pharmabench-2024.datasets: 156,618 raw records from 14,401 bioassays, curated into 52,482 records across 11 ADMET datasets.
pharmabench-2024.method: Language-model-assisted assay-information extraction, followed by curation of structures, units, duplicates and assay conditions, with modeling splits provided.
pharmabench-2024.conclusion: Harmonizes assay conditions and data processing to provide ADMET modeling datasets with clearer experimental context.
pharmabench-2024.evaluation: Benchmark construction focuses on assay conditions, units, structure cleaning and data splitting.
pharmabench-2024.limitations: The workflow can guide data cleaning and label harmonization. Merging with other public data requires duplicate checks by source and molecular structure.
pharmabench-2024.name: PharmaBench
pharmabench-2024.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.
pharmabench-2024.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, key sections of the paper and related official resources.

openadmet-avoidome-2026.one_liner: Proposes combining open experimental data, protein structures, active learning and blind challenges to improve mechanistic ADMET prediction.
openadmet-avoidome-2026.pain_point: Public ADMET data are scarce and assays inconsistent; limited structural mechanistic information constrains model-guided optimization.
openadmet-avoidome-2026.datasets: Discusses open, mechanism-oriented data generation and experimental plans involving CYPs, transporters, PXR and hERG.
openadmet-avoidome-2026.method: Connects high-throughput chemistry, functional assays, structural biology, active learning and blind challenges to study ADMET-related anti-targets.
openadmet-avoidome-2026.conclusion: Outlines a research program using open experimental data and mechanistic modeling to support multiparameter drug design.
openadmet-avoidome-2026.evaluation: This Perspective develops a research agenda around open data, mechanistic modeling and blind challenges.
openadmet-avoidome-2026.limitations: Provides context for OpenADMET's motivation and plans for CYP, transporter and safety-related mechanistic datasets.
openadmet-avoidome-2026.name: OpenADMET / Avoid-ome
openadmet-avoidome-2026.code_status: Links to the OpenADMET organization and its data, tools and challenge projects.
openadmet-avoidome-2026.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, key sections of the paper and related official resources.

maplight-2023.one_liner: Combines molecular fingerprints and descriptors in CatBoost models to assess the strength of conventional features for ADMET prediction.
maplight-2023.pain_point: Can simple, computationally inexpensive feature-based models remain competitive with deep learning?
maplight-2023.method: Combines ECFP, Avalon, ErG and molecular descriptors in CatBoost, with an additional variant incorporating GNN representations.
maplight-2023.conclusion: Fingerprint combinations perform well on multiple ADMET endpoints and provide useful baselines. A subsequent third-party audit reports that two MapLight variants passed its checks.
maplight-2023.evaluation: Evaluates model variants on 22 TDC ADMET tasks; a separate third-party preprint audits the reproducibility of two variants.
maplight-2023.limitations: Fingerprint combinations offer practical endpoint-modeling baselines. Read third-party audit results alongside the code versions and checks used.
maplight-2023.name: MapLight
maplight-2023.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.

tdc-audit-2026.name: TDC model audit
tdc-audit-2026.one_liner: Checks whether leading TDC models run, contain data leakage and reproduce their reported ADMET results.
tdc-audit-2026.pain_point: Leaderboard results may depend on pretraining leakage, validation/test overlap or environment problems that affect reproducibility.
tdc-audit-2026.datasets: 10 leading methods selected from the 22-task TDC ADMET benchmark, using the audit's leaderboard snapshot and code versions.
tdc-audit-2026.method: Sequentially checks environment availability, pretraining leakage, validation/test overlap and result reproduction.
tdc-audit-2026.conclusion: The authors report that only MapLight, MapLight+GNN and CaliciBoost pass all checks. CaliciBoost addresses Caco-2 specifically, rather than all 22 tasks.
tdc-audit-2026.evaluation: Audits 10 leading methods for execution, leakage, validation/test overlap and reproduction, recording the relevant leaderboard snapshot and code versions.
tdc-audit-2026.limitations: The audit separates environment failures from experimental-design issues and can inform reproduction workflows. These notes summarize the preprint's findings.
tdc-audit-2026.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.
tdc-audit-2026.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, abstract and accessible project documentation.

trimole-hybrid-2026.one_liner: Fuses sequences, molecular graphs, 3D structures and chemical priors, selecting prediction models or ensembles for each ADMET task.
trimole-hybrid-2026.pain_point: A single representation may not suit all endpoints; complementary modalities must be combined with a controlled model-selection process.
trimole-hybrid-2026.method: Combines SMILES, molecular graphs, 3D geometry and chemical priors with task-specific prediction heads, model selection and ensembles.
trimole-hybrid-2026.conclusion: Reports scores above the top entry on 10/22 tasks and within the top ten on 21/22 tasks in the selected public leaderboard snapshot.
trimole-hybrid-2026.evaluation: Evaluates multimodal combinations on 22 TDC tasks against the public leaderboard snapshot selected in the paper.
trimole-hybrid-2026.limitations: The repository provides implementation and review materials. Complete trained weights, official datasets and cached representations require separate preparation.

admet-evo-2026.one_liner: Uses a research agent to explore features and models for ADMET tasks, evaluating prediction and research efficiency through a fixed testing workflow.
admet-evo-2026.pain_point: Different endpoints need different features, models and optimization strategies, making repeated manual exploration costly. Automated research also needs test-independent model selection.
admet-evo-2026.datasets: 22 TDC ADMET tasks plus 43 toxicity tasks.
admet-evo-2026.method: An evidence-gated research agent explores hypotheses, features and models. The paper describes freezing the workflow before held-out testing and validation over multiple seeds.
admet-evo-2026.conclusion: Reports a task-normalized aggregate score of 96.77 and reduced cumulative model-fitting time under the stated comparisons and resource constraints.
admet-evo-2026.evaluation: Uses preprint v2, covering 22 TDC tasks and 43 toxicity tasks with the authors' task-normalized aggregate metric.

hergai-2025.one_liner: Combines docking and ensemble models to identify compounds likely to block the cardiac hERG ion channel in large candidate collections.
hergai-2025.pain_point: Small or positive-enriched test sets poorly represent screening collections containing many negatives and few hERG blockers.
hergai-2025.datasets: 299,927 curated PubChem/ChEMBL molecules: 1,937 positives and 297,990 negatives. Uses an IC50 threshold of 20 μM and an approximately 3:1 train/test allocation grouped by Bemis–Murcko scaffold.
hergai-2025.method: Selects poses after Smina docking and extracts protein–ligand PLEC fingerprints. RF, XGBoost and DNN base models feed a DNN stacking model; oversampling occurs within training folds.
hergai-2025.conclusion: Reports test recall of approximately 86% for blockers with IC50 ≤ 20 μM and 94% for those with IC50 ≤ 1 μM. Screening enrichment exceeds the generic docking scores compared in the paper.
hergai-2025.evaluation: Five-fold training-set cross-validation for tuning; reports recall, specificity, balanced accuracy and enrichment. The 86%/94% values are positive recall at two activity thresholds.
hergai-2025.limitations: Test-set screening performance informed the choice of pose-scoring scheme. High recall comes with false positives, so specificity and enrichment matter; the workflow also requires docking and structural fingerprint calculation.
hergai-2025.name: HERGAI
hergai-2025.code_status: Author code and data are accessible; the repository was archived on 2026-01-01.
hergai-2025.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, relevant methods and results, and the listed official resources.

publication.citation: Journal of Cheminformatics 17, 110; 2025-07-24

cardiotox-net-2021.one_liner: Combines neural-network predictions from different molecular representations to identify hERG blockers and tests them on three external datasets.
cardiotox-net-2021.pain_point: Single representations can omit relevant information, while simple model combinations struggle to balance sensitivity, specificity and predictive accuracy.
cardiotox-net-2021.datasets: 12,620 training molecules from BindingDB, ChEMBL and literature: 6,643 blockers and 5,977 non-blockers. Three external sets contain 44, 41 and 839 molecules, using an IC50 threshold of 10 μM.
cardiotox-net-2021.method: Five base neural networks process different chemical features; a separate neural network combines their predictions. A 70/10/10/10 allocation supports base-model training/validation and meta-model training/validation.
cardiotox-net-2021.conclusion: External MCC values are 0.599/0.452/0.220 and accuracies 0.810/0.755/0.746. Several metrics improve over selected earlier methods, but PPV on the third, imbalanced set is only 0.113.
cardiotox-net-2021.evaluation: The Data preparation section describes the training and three external datasets and analyzes their chemical similarity.
cardiotox-net-2021.limitations: Two external sets are small; the third has a low positive fraction. Its PPV of 0.113 highlights false positives under imbalance and should be read alongside recall.
cardiotox-net-2021.name: CardioTox net
cardiotox-net-2021.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.
cardiotox-net-2021.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, relevant methods and results, and the listed official resources.

bbb-megamolbart-2024.one_liner: Predicts blood–brain barrier permeability with a molecular language model and XGBoost, then tests selected compounds in human-derived 3D BBB spheroids.
bbb-megamolbart-2024.pain_point: BBB labels are limited; the study tests whether pretrained molecular representations improve prediction and receive experimental support in vitro.
bbb-megamolbart-2024.datasets: B3DB: 7,807 molecules (4,956 BBB+, 2,851 BBB−); CMUH: 2,499 (105 BBB+, 2,394 BBB−). B3DB includes 1,058 logBB values. Spheroid experiments select 21 predicted permeable and 5 predicted impermeable candidates, with controls.
bbb-megamolbart-2024.method: MegaMolBART encodes SMILES for XGBoost classification/regression, compared with Morgan fingerprints. BBB spheroids contain human brain microvascular endothelial cells, pericytes and astrocytes; LC–MS/MS measures permeability.
bbb-megamolbart-2024.conclusion: Reports a final held-out AUROC of 0.88. Spheroid results agree with prediction directions for the selected candidates, supporting exploratory BBB screening.
bbb-megamolbart-2024.evaluation: Compares B3DB-only training, CMUH external testing and mixed-data settings. The final classifier splits B3DB/CMUH 80/10/10, achieving held-out AUROC = 0.88.
bbb-megamolbart-2024.limitations: Spheroid experiments select candidates with very high or low scores, supporting their in vitro permeability classification. Intermediate-score compounds and human permeability need further experiments.
bbb-megamolbart-2024.name: BBB MegaMolBART
bbb-megamolbart-2024.code_status: The paper links B3DB and MegaMolBART components; a link to the complete training workflow remains to be added.
bbb-megamolbart-2024.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, relevant methods and results, and the listed official resources.

publication.citation: Scientific Reports 14, 15844; 2024-07-09

mc-pgp-2025.one_liner: Fuses SMILES, fingerprints and molecular graphs to separately predict P-gp inhibition and transport-substrate status.
mc-pgp-2025.pain_point: Single representations miss P-gp-related structural information. Inhibitors and substrates require distinct tasks and evaluation on compounds from new sources.
mc-pgp-2025.datasets: Public databases/literature: 5,943 molecules for inhibition (4,558 positives, 1,385 negatives) and 4,018 for substrate prediction (2,455 positives, 1,563 negatives). Independent external sets contain 140 and 185 molecules, respectively.
mc-pgp-2025.method: Attention fuses SMILES sequences, fingerprints and graphs. Graph contrastive learning aligns local and global structure, with analysis of relevant functional groups.
mc-pgp-2025.conclusion: External inhibitor AUROC is 0.906 ± 0.015. The authors report relative AUROC improvements of 9.82%/10.62% over the next-best method on the inhibitor/substrate external sets.
mc-pgp-2025.evaluation: Internal comparisons use random and scaffold splits; Tables 4–5 report external results. The 9.82%/10.62% values are relative AUROC improvements over the next-best method.
mc-pgp-2025.limitations: Inhibition and substrate status are evaluated separately, each with positive and negative examples. The corresponding TDC Pgp_Broccatelli task concerns inhibitor classification.
mc-pgp-2025.name: MC-PGP
mc-pgp-2025.code_status: Public availability of the complete training implementation remains to be verified.
mc-pgp-2025.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, relevant methods and results, and the listed official resources.

ames-multitask-2022.name: AMES multitask DNN
ames-multitask-2022.one_liner: Learns Ames outcomes for five bacterial strains jointly, retaining strain-specific information alongside the overall mutagenicity label.
ames-multitask-2022.pain_point: Collapsing results across strains into one label discards strain-level information useful for mutagenicity prediction.
ames-multitask-2022.datasets: Authors' Mendeley v2 data: 5,536 ISSSTY-curated molecules with 1,360 Mordred descriptors, labels for TA98, TA100, TA102, TA1535 and TA1537 plus Overall, including undetermined labels. Train/Internal/External partitions are provided.
ames-multitask-2022.method: A shared-representation multitask DNN learns five strain outcomes and is compared with overall-label single-task models, strain-specific models and their ensembles. Compounds with partially undetermined labels are retained.
ames-multitask-2022.conclusion: The published abstract reports improvements over overall-label single-task models and ensembles of strain-specific models, supporting the use of strain-level information.
ames-multitask-2022.evaluation: The authors' data.py provides Train/Internal/External partitions and five-fold cross-validation, stratifying multitask folds by Overall labels. Individual scores await checking against the published tables.
ames-multitask-2022.limitations: Five strain labels provide information about different mutation sensitivities. The code README retains submission-stage wording; citations use the published JCIM version.
ames-multitask-2022.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.
ames-multitask-2022.verification_scope: Published metadata/abstract, authors' Mendeley v2 documentation, code README and data.py; published result tables have not been fully checked.

publication.citation: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling 62(24), 6342–6351; online 2022-09-06.

amesnet-2026.one_liner: Combines molecular structure, bacterial strain and metabolic-activation conditions to improve Ames mutagenicity detection in unfamiliar chemical space.
amesnet-2026.pain_point: Models miss mutagenic compounds outside the training domain, while increasing sensitivity alone can produce many false positives.
amesnet-2026.datasets: Strain/S9-conditioned data compiled by Lui et al. After the published version's cleaning, training/validation contains 40,129 records and testing 4,208. Each record is a compound–strain–S9 combination. Foil data lacking strain/S9 information are evaluated separately.
amesnet-2026.method: A molecular encoder and strain/±S9 condition channel form two branches. Compares single-task, ordinary/grouped multitask models and condition-augmented encoders including ChemProp and GROVER.
amesnet-2026.conclusion: The published main OOD evaluation reports sensitivity 0.72 (95% CI 0.68–0.76) and balanced accuracy 0.81 (0.78–0.83). The supplementary Foil evaluation gives balanced accuracy 0.72.
amesnet-2026.evaluation: Uses the source study's OOD partitions and removes identical non-stereochemical SMILES across partitions. Main-task and Foil metrics are separate; international Ames/QSAR challenge results provide background comparisons.
amesnet-2026.limitations: The published test set contains 4,208 records with sensitivity 0.72; preprint v2 uses 4,528 and reports 0.73. The revision changes data cleaning; these notes use the published results.
amesnet-2026.name: AmesNet
amesnet-2026.code_status: TCL comparison models, predictions and statistical code are public, with some large files on Hugging Face. Availability of the complete AmesNet implementation and weights is unconfirmed.
amesnet-2026.verification_scope: Published metadata/abstract, searchable publisher methods, supplementary material, preprint v2 methods and author repository; continuous access to the ACS full text was restricted.

chemprop-dmpnn-2019.one_liner: Learns molecular representations by passing messages along directed chemical bonds and evaluates property prediction on public and industrial data.
chemprop-dmpnn-2019.pain_point: Evidence was limited on whether learned representations outperform handcrafted descriptors and generalize to industrial data and new chemical space.
chemprop-dmpnn-2019.datasets: 19 public and 16 private industrial datasets spanning multiple chemical endpoints.
chemprop-dmpnn-2019.method: Directed-bond message passing (D-MPNN), molecular-level computed features and hyperparameter optimization, compared with fixed descriptors and earlier graph networks.
chemprop-dmpnn-2019.conclusion: Matches or exceeds several baselines on the evaluated public/industrial tasks, demonstrating the practical value of learned representations. Performance remains below experimental reproducibility and varies by task and split.
chemprop-dmpnn-2019.evaluation: Compares random, scaffold and available temporal splits to assess generalization to new chemical space and industrial data.
chemprop-dmpnn-2019.limitations: The 2019 paper establishes Chemprop's methodological foundation. Later software development makes version, feature and split control important for reproduction.
chemprop-dmpnn-2019.name: Chemprop / D-MPNN
chemprop-dmpnn-2019.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.
chemprop-dmpnn-2019.verification_scope: Bibliographic metadata, relevant methods and results, and the listed official resources.

attentivefp-2019.one_liner: Learns which atoms and neighborhoods to emphasize when aggregating molecular information for property prediction and structural attribution.
attentivefp-2019.pain_point: Representations must capture local and longer-range structural relationships while making model-selected chemical features easier to inspect.
attentivefp-2019.datasets: The authors' repository provides BBBP, HIV, BACE, ClinTox, SIDER, Tox21, ToxCast, ESOL (delaney), FreeSolv (SAMPL), Lipophilicity, QM9 and aromaticity examples, covering ADMET, activity, physicochemical and quantum-chemical tasks.
attentivefp-2019.method: Attention in molecular-graph message aggregation and graph-level readout produces learned fingerprints; attention visualization explores structural information.
attentivefp-2019.conclusion: Reports advanced performance at publication on the tested tasks and visual examples of learned nonlocal intramolecular relationships.
attentivefp-2019.evaluation: The data directory includes classification, regression and aromaticity examples. Comparisons require aligned splits and training configurations.
attentivefp-2019.limitations: Attention visualizations show structures emphasized by the model. Online-date fields differ: Crossref/ACS page header gives 2019-08-13, while ACS history gives 2019-08-27; the catalog records the year.
attentivefp-2019.name: AttentiveFP
attentivefp-2019.code_status: Author code and accompanying data are accessible; rebuild the original Code Ocean environment following the reproduction instructions.
attentivefp-2019.verification_scope: Metadata and conflicting dates, original abstract, author implementation, data directory and REPRODUCING.md; dataset-level result tables have not been fully checked.

moleculenet-2018.one_liner: Brings molecular datasets, splits, metrics and algorithms into a shared benchmark for property prediction.
moleculenet-2018.pain_point: Different choices of datasets, metrics and implementations make model improvements difficult to separate from evaluation effects.
moleculenet-2018.datasets: Public quantum-chemical, physicochemical, biophysical and physiological datasets, including ESOL, FreeSolv, Lipophilicity, BBBP, Tox21, ClinTox, SIDER, BACE, HIV and QM collections, with task-specific metrics and splits.
moleculenet-2018.method: DeepChem data loaders, molecular featurizers and learning algorithms support systematic comparisons of fixed descriptors and learned representations.
moleculenet-2018.conclusion: Learned representations work across multiple tasks, while small datasets and imbalance remain challenging. Physically informed features can matter more than algorithm choice in quantum/biophysical tasks.
moleculenet-2018.evaluation: Metrics and splits are task-specific; comparisons should record the subset, data version, cleaning steps and split.
moleculenet-2018.limitations: Coverage includes ADMET, activity, physicochemical and quantum-chemical tasks. DeepChem loading workflows evolve. Publication metadata records the publisher's 2017-10-31 online date alongside the 2018 issue.
moleculenet-2018.name: MoleculeNet
moleculenet-2018.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.

moleculeace-2022.one_liner: Evaluates structurally similar molecules with large activity differences to expose model weaknesses hidden by average prediction errors.
moleculeace-2022.pain_point: Overall error does not adequately capture activity-cliff performance, which matters for lead optimization.
moleculeace-2022.datasets: Curated bioactivity datasets for 30 macromolecular targets, comparing 24 machine-learning strategies. The authors provide data and evaluation workflows.
moleculeace-2022.method: Defines structurally similar pairs with large activity differences and reports overall RMSE alongside cliff-molecule RMSEcliff, comparing descriptor models with graph/sequence neural networks.
moleculeace-2022.conclusion: Several descriptor-based methods outperform more complex deep models in the tested activity-cliff settings. Performance varies by target, supporting separate cliff metrics.
moleculeace-2022.evaluation: Analyzes overall RMSE and RMSEcliff with fixed data/code versions and cliff definitions. A 2023 correction revises the early-stopping description.
moleculeace-2022.limitations: The focus is bioactivity differences among similar structures. Original-paper and later implementation results are recorded separately to track changes in data and code.
moleculeace-2022.name: MoleculeACE
moleculeace-2022.code_status: The authors provide a public code/project page.

ssl-gcn-2021.name: SSL-GCN
ssl-gcn-2021.one_liner: Trains a graph neural network on labeled and unlabeled molecules to improve Tox21 toxicity prediction through semi-supervised learning.
ssl-gcn-2021.pain_point: Toxicity labels are limited, while many compounds have only structural information; supervised graph models cannot fully use these unlabeled molecules.
ssl-gcn-2021.datasets: Tox21: 7,831 molecules and 12 toxicity endpoints. Removing labels from ClinTox, SIDER, ToxCast and HIV and excluding structures overlapping with Tox21 yields 50,527 unlabeled molecules.
ssl-gcn-2021.method: A GCN encodes molecular graphs within a Mean Teacher framework. The student learns toxicity labels, teacher parameters follow an exponential moving average of student parameters, and prediction consistency under perturbations incorporates unlabeled data.
ssl-gcn-2021.conclusion: The paper reports a best mean ROC-AUC of 0.757, compared with about 0.71 for the conventional machine-learning models evaluated. Unlabeled data improve prediction, with the best mixing ratio varying by endpoint.
ssl-gcn-2021.evaluation: Tox21 uses an 80%/10%/10% scaffold split and five repeated runs. Comparisons include supervised SL-GCN, ECFP4-based KNN, neural networks, random forests, SVM and XGBoost, and DeepChem models. Tested unlabeled-to-labeled ratios are 0.5, 1, 2, 3 and 4.
ssl-gcn-2021.limitations: Label completeness and class balance vary across the 12 endpoints. Endpoint AUROC and mixing-ratio experiments show that adding more unlabeled molecules does not consistently improve every task.
ssl-gcn-2021.code_status: The author repository provides training and prediction scripts, with README links to data and model archives.
ssl-gcn-2021.verification_scope: Reviewed the publisher full text for data, scaffold splitting, Mean Teacher and results, and checked the author repository README.

uni-qsar-2023.name: Uni-QSAR
uni-qsar-2023.one_liner: Automatically combines fingerprints, descriptors and pretrained 1D, 2D and 3D molecular representations with tuning and stacked ensembles for ADMET prediction.
uni-qsar-2023.pain_point: Different properties favor different molecular features, making manual representation, model and hyperparameter selection costly; skewed regression labels and class imbalance add further modeling challenges.
uni-qsar-2023.datasets: The 22 TDC ADMET Benchmark Group tasks: nine regression and 13 classification tasks. A separate CNS penetration case uses 940 training compounds (315 positive and 625 negative) and 117 external test compounds.
uni-qsar-2023.method: Combines fingerprints and descriptors with 1D representations such as K-BERT, 2D representations including GROVER, MolCLR and KPGT, and Uni-Mol 3D representations. Target transformations, imbalance-aware learning, Bayesian optimization and two-level stacking are orchestrated with dflow.
uni-qsar-2023.conclusion: Tables 1–2 report Caco-2 MAE of 0.273 and BBBP AUROC of 0.925. Counting the printed TDC ranking rows gives 17 first-place results across 22 tasks. The CNS case reports AUROC of 0.980; ablations support the contributions of 3D representations, stacking and target transformations.
uni-qsar-2023.evaluation: TDC experiments follow the benchmark report cited in the paper and compare with Chemprop, DeepAutoQSAR and DeepPurpose; some baseline scores come from prior reports or leaderboards. Per-task splits and seeds are not detailed. Table 1 shows first place for 8/9 regression tasks and Table 2 for 9/13 classification tasks, as recorded in the paper.
uni-qsar-2023.limitations: The abstract claims SOTA on 21/22 tasks, whereas the TDC ranking rows in Tables 1–2 contain 17/22 first-place entries. These notes use the task metrics and rank counts in the tables; the paper does not reconcile the two counts.
uni-qsar-2023.code_status: The related public component, Uni-Mol Tools, provides Uni-Mol representations and property prediction, rather than the complete multi-representation stacking pipeline described in the paper.
uni-qsar-2023.verification_scope: Reviewed arXiv v1, Tables 1–2, the CNS case and ablations, and checked the Uni-Mol Tools README for its paper citation and documented features.
source_labels: Version 1 full text and result tables

domain-aware-pbrics-2023.name: Domain-aware / pBRICS
domain-aware-pbrics-2023.one_liner: Builds chemically meaningful molecular fragments so graph models can predict ADMET properties and identify fragments contributing to each prediction.
domain-aware-pbrics-2023.pain_point: Atom-level importance is difficult to translate into functional groups and medicinal-chemistry changes, while generic fragmentation can break chemically meaningful substructures.
domain-aware-pbrics-2023.datasets: 23 classification endpoints curated from ADMETlab 2.0 data, covering Ames mutagenicity, carcinogenicity, CYPs, eye and respiratory toxicity, BBBP and Tox21. ChEMBL molecules support fragmentation analysis; interpretation cases include 102 BBBP matched molecular pairs comprising 110 unique molecules.
domain-aware-pbrics-2023.method: pBRICS post-processes BRICS fragments using functional-group rules to organize scaffolds and substituents. MACCS and ECFP2 fragment fingerprints feed single-task and multitask GCN/RGCN models; Grad-CAM and matched molecular pairs examine fragment contributions.
domain-aware-pbrics-2023.conclusion: In Table 2, multitask fragment RGCN achieves mean AUROC of 84.47% across 23 endpoints, versus 83.35% for the comparator trained with ADMETlab 2.0 code, a gain of 1.12 percentage points. Fragment analyses connect functional-group changes with BBBP and Ames predictions.
domain-aware-pbrics-2023.evaluation: The train/validation/test ratio is 80%/10%/10%; the text does not specify random versus scaffold splitting. Table 2 compares MT-FraGCN, MT-FraRGCN, ST-FraGCN and the ADMETlab 2.0 comparator. Sections 3.3–3.4 examine BBBP and Ames matched molecular pairs.
domain-aware-pbrics-2023.limitations: Matched-pair analysis shows that scaffold correlations can dominate predictions: plausible local fragment attribution can coexist with an incorrect class prediction. The same team’s related pBRICS journal study (10.1021/acs.jcim.3c00689) covers 40 properties; the 23-task, 84.47% result here belongs to the workshop paper.
domain-aware-pbrics-2023.code_status: The paper and workshop listing do not provide an accompanying code link.
domain-aware-pbrics-2023.verification_scope: Reviewed the official acceptance listing and its linked 13-page PDF, including fragment representations, splitting, Table 2 and matched-pair analyses; also checked the related journal study’s metadata and task count.

ai-toxicity-review-2023.name: AI for drug toxicity: review
ai-toxicity-review-2023.one_liner: Surveys machine-learning and deep-learning approaches by toxicity task and collects public datasets and prediction tools for model development.
ai-toxicity-review-2023.pain_point: Toxicity research spans heterogeneous endpoints, data resources and models, creating a need for task-oriented routes to usable datasets, representative methods and tools.
ai-toxicity-review-2023.datasets: Covers six major toxicity properties and Tox21 endpoints. Supplementary Table S2 lists resources including Tox21, TOXRIC, ToxRefDB 2.0, DILIrank, ToxCast, CTD, PubChem, ChEMBL, OCHEM and TDC; database sizes are recorded as accessed on 2022-05-10.
ai-toxicity-review-2023.method: Reviews machine-learning algorithms and deep-learning architectures for toxicity prediction. Supplementary Table S1 compares Tox21 methods, input features and performance; S2 lists data sources; S3 catalogs tools, their model counts and algorithms.
ai-toxicity-review-2023.conclusion: Provides a task-oriented route to models, data and tools, covering fingerprint and descriptor models as well as graph networks, multitask and knowledge-guided methods. It offers a reading framework for a toxicity-prediction topic.
ai-toxicity-review-2023.evaluation: This is a review, with performance drawn from cited studies. Table S1 records features and AUC/ACC by method. Table S3 includes ProTox-II, FP-ADMET, HelixADMET and ADMETlab 2.0, with website access dated 2022-06-15.
ai-toxicity-review-2023.limitations: Table S1 scores reflect the endpoints and experimental settings of different original studies; model comparisons require those source papers. Database sizes, tool versions and access dates in Tables S2–S3 are retained as historical records.
ai-toxicity-review-2023.code_status: Associated resources are the public-data and prediction-tool lists in Supplementary Tables S2–S3.
ai-toxicity-review-2023.verification_scope: Reviewed publisher metadata and abstract and Tables S1–S3 in the authors’ public 17-page supporting information; the individual toxicity sections in the main text have not been checked in full.
